candidates.attacker_control: The `iri`, `lang`/`langtag`, `query`/`update` parameters of a GET to http://<fuseki>/$/validate/{iri,langtag,query,update} are fully attacker-controlled. A payload such as `?langtag=<script>...</script>` survives the validator's filter (the checks reject whitespace and '--' but not '<', '>', '"'), and `?iri=<script>...</script>` is echoed even when IRI creation throws. Payloads can be delivered by a malicious page (link/iframe/img/form) that makes the victim's browser request the local Fuseki server.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for a compensating control: (a) Shiro default shiro.ini restricts `/$/**` to the localhost filter; however LocalhostFilter/LocalhostOnly compare request.getRemoteAddr() against 127.0.0.1/[::1], which a browser on the same host satisfies, so it does not prevent a browser-driven XSS (it only blocks direct remote requests). (b) ValidatorHtmlLib.htmlQuote exists and DataValidatorHTML/output() do escape; the vulnerable paths demonstrably do not call it. (c) Query text echoes are escaped via output(); only error strings remain unescaped there. (d) Validators are part of standard UI/main module registration (FMod_UI / FusekiMain), not a test-only path. (e) Considered whether the response is JSON by default: ValidatorBase chooses JSON only when the Accept negotiation matches application/json; browsers negotiate to text/html, hitting the vulnerable path.
candidates.impact: Script execution in the Fuseki origin via a crafted link/iframe. Because the admin API is same-origin and localhost-restricted only, the injected script can create/delete datasets, trigger backups/compaction, enumerate datasets and read/modify data in a locally running Fuseki (drive-by attack). If the endpoint is exposed beyond localhost (or the deployment relies on the localhost rule), the attack is remotely triggerable by any site the victim visits.
candidates.prerequisites: Fuseki is reachable from the victim's browser (the normal local/desktop deployment; the browser is the loopback client, so Shiro's LocalhostFilter sees getRemoteAddr()=127.0.0.1 and allows the request). The validator servlets must be registered, which is the default when the UI module is present (FMod_UI registers /$/validate/query|update|iri|langtag|data and enables stats; FusekiMain does the same when serverArgs.validators is set). No authentication is required because the validators are under /$/ and the default shiro.ini only restricts /$/ to localhost, not to authenticated users.
candidates.root_cause: Fuseki's HTML validators render attacker-controlled request parameters and parser error text directly into an HTML response without applying the package's own HTML escaping (ValidatorHtmlLib.htmlQuote). LangTagValidatorHTML prints the raw `langtag`/`lang` parameter (and the raw formatted parts) after only syntactic checks that do not reject '<'/'>', and IRIValidatorHTML prints the raw `iri` parameter and IRI violation/exception text. QueryValidatorHTML/UpdateValidatorHTML escape the echoed query via ValidatorHtmlLib.output(), but print `ex.getMessage()` (which can quote input-derived tokens) unescaped.
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in Fuseki validator HTML reports (unescaped request parameters/error messages in text/html responses)
candidates.trace: 1) Victim visits attacker page. 2) Page navigates/iframes http://localhost:3030/$/validate/langtag?langtag=%3Cscript%3E...%3C/script%3E. 3) Dispatcher routes /$/validate/langtag to LangTagValidator -> ValidatorBase.execute(); browser Accept selects executeHTML(). 4) LangTagValidatorHTML.executeHTML() prints the raw parameter at line 87 (and raw formatted values via print(), line 139) after ValidatorHtmlLib.setHeaders() set Content-Type text/html. 5) Browser parses the response as HTML and executes the script in the Fuseki origin. 6) Same-origin script can call localhost-allowed admin endpoints such as POST/DELETE /$/datasets (manager operations) and read/exfiltrate dataset contents.
candidates.unverified: Runtime reachability and exploitability were not executed (read-only review; no tests run). The exact upstream fix commit/CWE label for this snapshot is unknown; escaping behavior may differ for some deployments if the UI/validators are disabled or a custom Shiro policy/CSRF proxy intervenes. HTML parsing/mutation of the exact payload after ServletOutputStream encoding was not executed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Coverage: the snapshot is Apache Jena 5.5.0-SNAPSHOT (CHANGES top entry 5.4.0, 2025-04-27), 5,231 files of which 4,788 are Java, across jena-core, jena-arq, jena-fuseki2 (core/main/webapp/access/mod-geosparql/ui), jena-geosparql, jena-iri/jena-iri3986, jena-langtag, jena-tdb1/tdb2, jena-db, jena-text, jena-permissions, jena-shacl/shex, extras. I inspected: all XML parser construction sites; Fuseki servlets/filters (AuthFilter, FusekiFilter, Dispatcher, LocalhostOnly, FMod_Admin/FMod_Shiro/FMod_UI, validators, DataUploader, ActionDatasets/Backup, SpatialIndexerService); HTTP auth and redirect policy; CORS filter; process/file utilities (ProcessUtils, Backup.chooseFileName, DataUploader); and deserialization sites (ObjectInputStream, Kryo). P1 relation-index scope: index_status partial (5,159 indexed files, 72 source files missing from the index, 4,788 Java parsed, 77,447 unresolved calls), no control-flow/data-flow, no semantic resolution, Spring annotation candidates unverified; index facts were used only for navigation and every candidate was re-checked against source text. Files were read via bounded ranges and targeted searches; this is a directed review, not exhaustive line-by-line coverage of all 5,231 files.
limitations: No code execution, tests, scanners or runtime probing were performed; all findings are static source-level leads.

The P1 relation index is partial (72 source files absent) and offers only syntactic call/containment/inheritance candidates with no data-flow or reachability proof, so some attacker-controlled flows may be missed.
The exact upstream fix commit / CVE / CWE label for this snapshot could not be identified from inside the source tree, so the intended benchmark issue may differ from the reported candidate.

The reported XSS assumes a browser-based victim can reach the Fuseki server; deployment-level mitigations (disabling the UI/validators, reverse proxy with authentication, custom Shiro policy, browser-side protections) were not verifiable statically.
Dependency versions and bundled JS assets were not exhaustively audited for known-vulnerable components.

rejected_leads.lead: Permissive CORS by default in Fuseki (ServerArgs.withCORS = true; FusekiServer corsInitParamsDft uses allowedOrigins=* and does not set allowCredentials, while the copied Jetty CrossOriginFilter defaults allowCredentials=true and echoes the request Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true)
rejected_leads.reason: Looks security-relevant (cross-origin credentialed reads when auth is configured), but the code and comments (--no-cors option, CHANGES 'Configurable CORS headers for Fuseki', defaults mirroring Jetty) indicate CORS-on-by-default is intentional upstream behavior, and the admin area is protected by the default shiro.ini. Not the strongest candidate; also depends on the victim having credentials for the Fuseki server.

rejected_leads.lead: LocalhostOnly servlet filter (jena-fuseki-main .../mod/admin/LocalhostOnly.java) is defined but never registered anywhere
rejected_leads.reason: Dead code / defense-in-depth gap only: the default shiro.ini (copied to FUSEKI_BASE by FusekiServerCtl and loaded by FMod_Shiro) already applies org.apache.jena.fuseki.authz.LocalhostFilter to /$/**; no reachable bypass demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: LangTagRE.str() stores the constructor string but returns null (jena-langtag .../LangTagRE.java:40-43)
rejected_leads.reason: Contract violation and possible NPE, but LangTagRE has no callers in the source tree (SysLangTag uses LangTagRFC5646); dead code, no attacker-reachable impact.
Wrong return value, but the method has no callers in the tree; no security impact demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: Java serialization / Kryo deserialization of spatial index files (jena-geosparql SpatialIndexV1 ObjectInputStream, SpatialIndexIoKryo Class.forName + Kryo readObject)
rejected_leads.reason: Prerequisite is local control of a configured index file; not reachable from the HTTP request path (the Fuseki spatial-indexer service writes/rewrites the file itself), so not a remotely exploitable deserialization bug on the evidence available.

All XML parsers I traced route through hardened factories (JenaXMLInput.createXMLReader with external-general/parameter entities and external DTDs disabled; SysRRX/JenaXMLInput StAX with SUPPORT_DTD/external-entity handling; GMLReader SAXBuilder with disallow-doctype-decl), so no unhardened parse path was found. XMLLiteralType relies on FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING with an explicit comment that external entities raise SAXParseException.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Jena 5.5.0-SNAPSHOT tree (5,231 files; 4,788 Java) for a defensive vulnerability assessment, tracing attacker-controlled inputs through Fuseki HTTP servlets, the RIOT/StAX XML parsers, GeoSPARQL, HTTP auth and process/file utilities. The strongest evidence-backed candidate is a reflected XSS (CWE-79) in the Fuseki `/$/validate/*` HTML report pages: user-controlled request parameters (and parser error messages) are written unescaped into a `text/html` response, even though an escaping helper exists in the same package and is applied elsewhere. The default Shiro `/$/** = localhostFilter` is not a compensating control for a browser-based attack because the victim's browser connects from 127.0.0.1, and the injected script then runs in the Fuseki origin, where the same localhost-only admin endpoints (`/$/datasets`, etc.) are also reachable. Other suspicious items (permissive CORS defaults, an unused LocalhostOnly filter, dead-code null/wrong returns, index-file deserialization) were rejected or kept as unconfirmed leads.
